title: Find Google Search results for a research question
description:
Build a reference list before writing a technical brief. Enter a query such as site:docs.python.org asyncio. Each bundle contains a title, URL, snippet and position; map link and title into your destination after this search.

Setup: install the FlashData app, select your own connection and configure the inputs. Create an API key at https://flashdata.dev/app/api-keys with this source enabled.

Country, interface language and location change the requested search context. Optional fields can be absent. This searches results; it does not fetch full article text. Maximum paid pages defaults to 1. Increasing it adds separately charged calls; Limit stops the output once reached.

Templates and the integration are free to install. FlashData API requests are paid; Make charges separately. Pricing: https://flashdata.dev/pricing
API and fields: https://flashdata.dev/docs/sources/google_search

title: Find YouTube videos by keyword
description:
Discover candidate videos for a topic such as python tutorial. Enter a query and a result limit up to 20. Each bundle includes a videoId, title, channel, duration, view count and available thumbnails. Add any paid enrichment step deliberately: it runs for every bundle.

Setup: install the FlashData app, select your own connection and configure the inputs. Create an API key at https://flashdata.dev/app/api-keys with this source enabled.

Search filters can select upload date, duration, type, sort order or features. Missing dates and counts stay unavailable. One run makes one paid request; there is no page token.

title: Get a YouTube transcript with timestamps
description:
Retrieve existing automatic captions for a known YouTube video in a chosen language. Map fullText into your own document or analysis step, or use segments with start/end seconds to build timestamped references. The template selects automatic captions explicitly.

Setup: install the FlashData app, select your own connection and configure the inputs. Create an API key at https://flashdata.dev/app/api-keys with this source enabled.

The language and automatic caption track must exist. FlashData does not run speech recognition, translate text or fall back to uploader captions. Installing this template does not include a language model.

Templates and the integration are free to install. FlashData API requests are paid; Make charges separately. Pricing: https://flashdata.dev/pricing
API and fields: https://flashdata.dev/docs/sources/youtube_transcript

title: Retrieve uploader-provided YouTube captions
description:
Read a video creator's existing caption track for a chosen language. The template explicitly selects uploader captions, returning languageCode, isAutoGenerated, timestamped segments and fullText. Use segments when exact caption timing matters.

Setup: install the FlashData app, select your own connection and configure the inputs. Create an API key at https://flashdata.dev/app/api-keys with this source enabled.

A missing uploader track returns an error; the workflow does not substitute automatic captions. No transcription or translation is performed. Choose the transcript template when you intend automatic captions.

title: Check YouTube Creative Commons license metadata
description:
Inspect the license label for a known video before your own rights review. Enter the video ID; the response includes videoId, kind, etag and permitted. A detected Creative Commons label yields ["all"]; other or missing metadata yields ["none"].

Setup: install the FlashData app, select your own connection and configure the inputs. Create an API key at https://flashdata.dev/app/api-keys with this source enabled.

The API source is called youtube_trainability, but this checks license metadata only. It does not report creator third-party-training settings or grant permission to train, download or reuse a video.

title: Deliver YouTube video or audio to your cloud storage
description:
Submit a video ID with your own writable storage destination. Choose video/audio format and optional clip times. The workflow returns a job ID and reads status once. If completed, it reads the JSON manifest containing file_url, file_size and downloaded_bytes.

Setup: install the FlashData app, select your own connection and configure the inputs. Create an API key at https://flashdata.dev/app/api-keys with this source enabled.

The S3 example contains nonfunctional placeholders. Replace them with your own private storage configuration before running. If processing, keep the job ID and use the companion reader later; do not resubmit. Downloads are charged by delivered bytes. File privacy and retention follow your storage configuration.

Templates and the integration are free to install. FlashData API requests are paid; Make charges separately. Pricing: https://flashdata.dev/pricing
API and fields: https://flashdata.dev/docs/sources/youtube_download
scenarioDescription: Submit one YouTube download to your own storage, read its status once, and retrieve the manifest if completed. Keep the job ID to check later without repeating the paid submission.
